Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

seem verb

also it seems, it seems to me, appear to, it looks that way to me, so it seems

classical

Cic. Off. 1.83: ut imbellēs timidīque videāmur
Traupman 376

videor, vidērī, vīsus sum

verb, second conjugation: the passive of videō, with a nominative and infinitive

seem, appear (to be or to do)

Latin makes the person or thing the subject: vidēris fessus esse, “you seem tired”. The impersonal vidētur with an accusative and infinitive is rare (Lewis & Short). Ut vidētur, as it seems (Traupman 27).

Other words

  • mihi vidētur — it seems to me, I think

    phrase: the person in the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 27: ā nātūrā mihi vidētur potius quam ab indigentiā orta amīcitia (Lewis & Short); Traupman 148, 184; Traupman 102: ita mihi vidētur

    With sī, the polite form of a suggestion: sī tibi vidētur, if you agree.

Examples

  • nōn semper ea sunt quae videntur

    things are not always what they seemPhaedr. 4.2.5

  • nunc ego tibi īrāscī videor?

    do I seem angry to you now?Gell. 1.26.8

  • quia videor ācer, alligant mē interdiū

    because I seem fierce, they tie me up by dayPhaedr. 3.7.15–20

  • aliquid natābat quod prīmō aspectū alga ipsa vidēbātur

    something was swimming that at first sight seemed to be the seaweed itselfLibellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

See also suggest, believe, I think so, appear.
